q: What does ISO 14068-1 require before a company can claim carbon neutrality?
title: ISO 14068-1 carbon neutral requirements
short: ISO 14068-1:2023 requires a defined subject and boundary, a quantified carbon footprint, a carbon neutrality management plan with reduction targets, cutting emissions before offsetting, offsetting only the residual with quality credits that are retired, and a claim that states the subject, period and how it was checked.
audience: Sustainability leads and exporters planning a claim

sections.h: The steps the standard sets out
ol: Define the subject of the claim: the whole organisation, a site, a product or an event, and its boundary.
Quantify its carbon footprint using a recognised method, for example ISO 14064-1 for an organisation or ISO 14067 for a product, including significant Scope 3 emissions.
Write a carbon neutrality management plan: a commitment, reduction targets with dates, the actions to meet them, and how progress is tracked.
Reduce emissions first. Offsetting comes after the planned reductions, never instead of them.
Counterbalance the residual emissions for the period with carbon credits that are retired, and report them.
Make the claim with its qualifiers: subject, period, footprint, reductions achieved, credits used, and the type of check behind it.

ul: Additional: the reduction or removal would not have happened without the credit revenue.
Permanent, or with reversal risk managed for removals that could be released again.
Not double counted, so the same tonne is not claimed by the host country or another buyer.
Verified by an independent body under a recognised programme, and retired in a registry for your claim.
The standard also expects a growing share of removals over time, in line with a transition to net zero.

p: BSI has said ISO 14068-1 replaces PAS 2060 and set a transition period for claims already made under PAS 2060. New claims should be made under ISO 14068-1. If you hold a PAS 2060 claim, check BSI's notice for the date it stops being valid and plan the move before your next claim period.

sections.h: Claims to EU consumers need extra care
p: From 27 September 2026, Directive (EU) 2024/825 bans claims to consumers that a product has a neutral, reduced or positive climate impact when the claim rests on offsetting. An ISO 14068-1 claim about your company can still be made to business buyers, but do not put a carbon neutral label on goods sold to EU consumers on the strength of credits.

The standard allows different levels of checking, from a self-declaration to independent third-party verification, and the claim must say which one applies. For an export buyer or a public claim, expect to be asked for third-party verification of both the footprint and the credits.

senseible: Senseible builds the Scope 1 and 2 part of the footprint from fuel and electricity invoices, with each line traced to its document, and keeps Scope 3 lines as a separate evidence trail. It does not retire credits, write the management plan or verify a carbon neutral claim.
